_: Golden behaviour of the Python `multilab` command, captured 13 October 2026 BEFORE porting it.
Trap-1 mitigation from docs/labs/d30-no-python-2026-10-13: parity.py compares Rust against
Python, so it dies when Python does. Once multilab is Rust there is no second opinion, so the
behaviour that mattered is frozen here and asserted by crates/uor-r4-harness/src/multilab.rs.
Captured by running the Python harness against a throwaway git repo with an empty claims store and
an isolated live tier. Timestamps, hostnames and paths are environment-dependent and asserted by
SHAPE; every other field is asserted exactly.

touch_defaults._branch: the current git branch, or empty when detached
touch_defaults._updated: ISO 8601 with the LOCAL offset, e.g. 2026-10-13T13:54:41-04:00

touch_writes_to: the LIVE tier only: <live>/presence/<lab>.json - never a checkout (R10)

rules_that_are_not_obvious.touch_preserves_what_the_lab_is_doing: touch exists for hooks - it refreshes the TIMESTAMP and must NOT blank `doing`/`milestone`/`next` that a heartbeat set. Blanking them would make a hook-driven lab look idle.
rules_that_are_not_obvious.source_says_which_tier_answered: source is `live` for a live-tier entry and `committed` for the durable fallback, so a reader can tell real-time from stale
rules_that_are_not_obvious.state_is_derived: state is `live (Nm ago)` or `STALE (Nm ago)` from PRESENCE_TTL_MINUTES, computed at read time, never stored
rules_that_are_not_obvious.live_wins_over_committed: when both tiers hold a lab, the live entry is shown and source says live
rules_that_are_not_obvious.committed_is_the_fallback: a lab with no live entry but a committed presence file is still shown, with source=committed
